decisions.reason: Fouling detection automation is tied to R&D and funded research and fits the announced digital efficiency direction, so management persists and attributes slow uptake to long municipal procurement cycles.
The weir dimensioning web tool is cheap to maintain, supports the core flood-control business, and generates leads with planners, so there is no reason to withdraw it.
As the hardware counterpart to Product A and a visible part of the energy-efficiency push, the fouling detection system will be kept, with weak early results treated as temporary market development.
The spring-controlled flap weir is close to the established hydraulic steelwork offer and was only launched in 2024, so management stands by it.
The energy management system is central to the announced direction of digitally networked, energy-efficient water infrastructure, making withdrawal very unlikely.
The overflow flap gate line has its own page and several models, signalling strong public commitment and close fit with the core business.
